criterion: The verdicts it produces are identical to the pairwise version for every ordering, including sessions whose bounds are missing or reversed
summary: Reviewer checked the structural argument against _overlaps' body and confirmed the reduction, including that a reversed window removes a session from its own candidate set, then measured each sub-claim separately rather than accepting it: the bisection selects exactly the candidate set over 80,214 checks with zero mismatches, the candidate reduction agrees with any-pair truth over the same, the prefix maxima recomputed by sorting agree over 37,392, and across 543,000 self-exclusion decisions the sweep never picked a session against itself and never missed a real partner. Its own brute force - its own predicate and its own loop, not the one in the test file - ran 121,290 cases with 0 disagreements: exhaustive over sizes 0-4 with a 15-window pool, exhaustive at size 5 with a 9-window pool, plus 8,000 randomised groups of 6-40, covering touching endpoints, identical and zero-width windows, reversed bounds, missing bounds, empty strings, and non-string bounds of type int, float, bool and dict. _bounded proved equal to _overlaps' four-way isinstance gate by re-association and confirmed over 20,740 pair combinations. One divergence found and recorded as a note: when the same dict object occupies two list slots the old loop skipped by identity and the sweep excludes by index, so both slots are flagged - unreachable from report, which builds a fresh dict per verdict, and arguably the better answer.
